changes.summary: six Atomic::fetch_update calls renamed to Atomic::try_update

compatibility.claim: The rename to try_update does not force a forward-only commitment: try_update is present and compiles on BOTH 1.98.1 and 1.99.0. Only the old name, fetch_update, is deprecated on 1.99.0 and therefore fails under the workspace policy of deny-warnings; the new name is valid on either toolchain.
compatibility.method: std-level compile probe of the exact expression shape used at the six call sites, compiled with `rustc <tc> --edition 2021 -D warnings --emit=metadata`. Files: target/tmp/t05probe/try_update.rs and target/tmp/t05probe/fetch_update.rs (scratch, gitignored).

toolchain_duplication_cost.claim: A second installed toolchain does not replace the first toolchain's artifacts; cargo namespaces both the fingerprint and the artifact filename by the rustc hash, so the same crate built under two toolchains coexists on disk. Building the same crates a second time under a second toolchain adds roughly one more artifact set.
toolchain_duplication_cost.mechanism: target/debug/.fingerprint/<crate>-<hash>/lib-<crate>.json carries a `rustc` field. Two toolchains produce two different `rustc` hashes, hence two fingerprint directories and two artifact filenames (libkg_ontology-<hash>.rlib). Direct evidence below.
toolchain_duplication_cost.method: An isolated CARGO_TARGET_DIR (target/tmp/t05dupe, removed from the main target/ namespace) was built first with 1.98.1 and then with 1.99.0, building the same crate and profile (kg-ontology --lib, dev profile, plus its dependencies) into the same directory. Sizes are apparent bytes (`du -sb`).
toolchain_duplication_cost.sample: kg-ontology (lib, dev profile + its dependency set)

direct_artifact_proof.fingerprint_basis: rustc fingerprint 5244445300240561903 is the value observed for kg-ontology in the main target/, which is built by the default 1.99.0 toolchain; the other hash is therefore the 1.98.1 build.

live_tree_context.note: The live target/ is ~10.7 GB and, per T01, already carries a 3.12x rlib duplication factor (1238 rlibs over 397 distinct crates). A second toolchain adds a further artifact set on top of that. This is why T03 closeout must reclaim through per-package `cargo clean` (which removes target artifacts) and not only through the content-addressed cache GC, which only releases derived store entries.

failure_modes.question: What breaks when dependencies fail?

paths.behavior: `rustup run <tc> rustc` / `cargo +<tc>` exits non-zero with `toolchain 'X' is not installed`. The record names the exact resolved toolchain for every claim, so an absent toolchain fails loudly rather than being silently substituted.

paths.failure: workspace crate emits a denied lint under -D warnings
paths.behavior: exit_code != 0 and no `Finished` line in the log. The gate log is preserved at target/tmp/t05_clippy_199.log with counted errors, so a failure is visible rather than inferred.
paths.observed: exit_code 0, errors 0 (the 48 warnings are vendor-dep lints capped by --no-deps)

paths.behavior: cargo exits non-zero and the build stops; because the resource under test is disk, the record captures the exact per-toolchain byte cost up front and notes that the machine had ~30 GB free, making the second-toolchain cost measurable before it is paid again.

The rename introduces no new dependency: it uses `std`. async-trait was already in the lockfile; the patch bump changes only the resolved version. All builds at record time used the already-resolved lock, so no network dependency is added by this transition.

failure_modes.negative_control: fetch_update under -D warnings on 1.99.0 exits 1, proving the deprecation path is enforced (not just declared).

load_profile.question: What saturates first at 10x?
load_profile.reasoning: This task is an evidence record, not a runtime service. Its resource dimension is the build cache: at 1x, one toolchain's artifact set for the sampled crates was 116.0 MB and the tree's target/ is ~10.7 GB; at 10x toolchain/feature combinations the artifact sets coexist (cargo namespaces by rustc/feature fingerprint), so disk saturates first, not CPU or memory.
load_profile.protection: T03 wires the closeout reclamation (`retention.target_cap_gb: 60` as DATA) into slice close and uses both mechanisms: content-addressed cache GC plus per-package `cargo clean`, which is the path that frees what a second toolchain duplicates.
load_profile.measured_saturation_input: second toolchain adds 0.78x of the single-toolchain artifact set (86.85 MiB added on 110.68 MiB)
